clue.text: One in store dashed round to deliver embroidered satin

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the first word encloses what follows
embroidery works threads into a new pattern, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: shot off means dashed away at speed
to pass something on is to deliver it
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone races off to hand over a piece of decorated satin cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' is not the courier's job here: to pass a thing on is to deliver it, and 'dashed' means shot off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person serving customers behind the counter works inside a retail outlet, hence one in a store.

clue.text: Teacher's sharp boost

blocks.note: the head is the senior teacher of a school, with the possessive S
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's quick, sharp encouragement to a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An early advantage given to someone at the start of a race or venture is a boost to their chances.

clue.text: Aim for a score

blocks.note: first meaning: to direct something, as a gun, at a target
second meaning: a unit counted in a game's tally

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests aiming to reach a total of twenty; 'score' is instead a unit won in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: You aim a weapon when you train it on a target, and each mark won in a match counts as one.

clue.text: The doctors sent up in South African dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top
one group is placed inside the letters of the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for South Africa
the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body

explanation.surface: Medics are mocked at a dance in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BMA is the British Medical Association, so 'the doctors' collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Brazilian ballroom style is a well-known dance.

clue.text: I am one to be treated, but not prepared to wait

blocks.note: the contraction I'm
a person receiving medical treatment

explanation.surface: A sick person in the waiting room has run out of patience.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a patient should be patient, yet this one is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and eager for things to happen now is unwilling to wait.

clue.text: The evidence could be old or new

blocks.note: first meaning: proof or tribute
second meaning: either half of the Christian Bible

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old or new' reads like a remark about the age of the evidence, but points to the two parts of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means proof of something, and the Bible divides into Old and New sections bearing that name.

clue.text: One is in part of church that's artless

indicators.note: something that is in a place sits inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: the main body of a church building
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in a church aisle is described as unsophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent, unworldly person lacks guile or sophistication, so is artless.

clue.text: Light blow shouldn't affect it

blocks.note: surface reading: a gentle tap will do it no harm
setter's reading: a lamp whose flame is shielded so even a storm cannot put it out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is the noun (a lamp) and 'blow' the wind, not a gentle knock.
explanation.definitionFit: This lantern has a glass chimney protecting the flame, so it stays lit in strong wind.

clue.text: London feature holds item in newspaper

blocks.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold, here plural
a regular article or section of a paper

explanation.surface: A London landmark is said to contain an article from the press.
explanation.walkthrough: A nelson (full or half) is a wrestling hold; the monument stands in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: The monument to Admiral Nelson in Trafalgar Square is a famous landmark of the capital.

clue.text: One with brain about to become university element

indicators.note: one letter is turned into another, swapping it out in the word

blocks.note: the skull, the thing that holds the brain
c. for circa, meaning about
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A clever person seems about to be made into a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The C of CRANIUM is replaced by U.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive metal is a chemical element, used as nuclear fuel.

clue.text: VIP's sea travels producing no reaction

indicators.note: letters that travel move about and land in a new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dignitary's sea voyage gets no response.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inert and unresponsive, acting on nothing, fails to produce any reaction.

clue.text: Exam mostly set in a different place

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to resite is to locate somewhere else

explanation.surface: A test is held mostly in a different venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A second attempt at a failed test is itself a test that students sit.

clue.text: They have particular interest in the workers!

definitions.text: They have particular interest in the workers!

blocks.clueFragment: They have particular interest in the workers!
blocks.note: surface reading: managers or unions concerned about staff

blocks.clueFragment: They have particular interest in the workers!
blocks.note: setter's reading: animals that feed on worker ants

explanation.walkthrough: Workers here are worker ants, and the interest is an appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-snouted mammals live by eating ants and termites, so worker insects are their food.

clue.text: Get along without power at the seaside

blocks.note: first meaning: move freely without engine drive, as a freewheeling bike
second meaning: the shore

explanation.surface: Managing without electricity on a seaside holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle freewheels with the engine off, and the land beside the sea is the shore.

clue.text: It's the end for four months

definitions.text: It's the end for four months

blocks.clueFragment: It's the end for four months
blocks.note: surface reading: something finishes after a four-month spell

blocks.clueFragment: It's the end for four months
blocks.note: setter's reading: the last day of April, June, September and November

explanation.walkthrough: Thirty days hath September, April, June and November.
explanation.definitionFit: Four months of the year have thirty days, so their final day carries this ordinal.

clue.text: Immediately used phone? True!

indicators.note: letters that have been used are worn and knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that they grabbed the phone at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The old-fashioned adverb means straight after that, at once, so immediately.

clue.text: Endlessly tired horse confused speculator

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter of the word is cut off
confused letters are muddled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weary, muddled horse is like a gambler on the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms theories speculates about how things work.

clue.text: With a wide view find duck and animal in the grass

indicators.note: the first items are placed inside the following word

blocks.note: panic grass is a type of grass (genus Panicum)
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O
a male sheep

explanation.surface: A broad vista reveals a duck and another creature in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping outlook taking in the whole scene is a panoramic one.

clue.text: Teachers taking in cut aim mainly for sustenance

indicators.note: to take something in is to enclose it within yourself
mainly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the National Union of Teachers
to trim is to cut
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Teachers trim their goals for the sake of sustenance.
explanation.walkthrough: NUT, the British teachers' union, holds TRIM and most of END.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that nourishes the body provides nourishment, or sustenance.

clue.text: An addition to the spirits is invigorating

blocks.note: first meaning: a quinine mixer added to gin
second meaning: restorative, bracing

explanation.surface: Something that lifts the mood is refreshing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like mood but means alcoholic drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinine water is mixed with gin, and a bracing, restoring thing is also described by this word.

clue.text: Large suit being woven gets slurs

indicators.note: weaving threads them together in a new pattern, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A big suit being made at the loom attracts insults.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation a curved line binding notes is called a slur or tie, also known by this name.

clue.text: Good kind of fabric to sparkle

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A quality cloth with a shine to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash or gleam with small bright reflections is to sparkle.

clue.text: Demonstrated how between bridge partners

indicators.note: placed between two things means set inside them

blocks.note: South and North, partners at the bridge table
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridge pair is taught technique at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demonstrated has been displayed or exhibited to others.

clue.text: The danger of a topper - ill-balanced, etc

indicators.note: the letters are taken from part of the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding completing the picture of a wobbling top hat

explanation.surface: A top hat perched precariously risks falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril and danger are synonyms for a risk of harm.

clue.text: Some trumpet item of little important in law

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Part of a trumpet is a minor legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal French adjective means small or minor, as in petit larceny or petit jury.

clue.text: Young ladies at Lord's?

blocks.note: first meaning: unmarried girls
second meaning: overs in cricket with no runs scored

explanation.surface: Debutantes are presented in a noble household.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a maiden is an over bowled without conceding a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried girls are maidens, and in cricket a scoreless over is a maiden.

clue.text: Choose one relation to be best

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
Roman numeral one
a mother is a relation

explanation.surface: Deciding which family member is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The most favourable or ideal condition is the best possible one.

clue.text: With little warning by the ad?

blocks.note: first meaning: suddenly, without time to prepare
second meaning: next to a brief printed announcement

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase places something beside a brief advertisement, which is a short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suddenly, with hardly any advance warning given.
